narrative:
The model determined that you have a 59% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeds the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the level of savings you have, and the purpose of the loan. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single biggest reason for the rejection. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% have a negative balance, while 59% have no checking account at all. This status strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk.

Your lack of savings (unknown or none) was the second most important factor, but it actually worked in your favor by pulling the prediction slightly toward approval. Most approved applicants also show limited or no documented savings, so this was not a negative signal.

The fact that you are requesting the loan to buy a new car was the third most influential element and increased the risk assessment. Only 16.5% of approved loans are for new cars, compared with 35% for radio or TV purchases, suggesting the bank views car loans as higher risk in this context.

To improve your chances next time, focus on building a positive checking account balance before reapplying, consider a smaller or differently purposed loan, and explore ways to demonstrate reliable savings. These steps would directly address the main reasons behind this decision. (218 words)
